item.title: Mini Crackme: Caesar-Shift Password Check (Windows x86-64)
item.description:
Target: Windows x86-64. check_password takes a 4-byte ASCII string in rcx (Windows x64: first arg in rcx). Find an input that makes it return 1.
check_password PROC lea r9, target ; r9 -> expected cipher bytes xor r8d, r8d ; i = 0 .top: cmp r8d, 4 jge .pass movzx edx, byte ptr [rcx+r8] ; edx = input[i] add edx, 3 ; Caesar shift +3 cmp edx, 'Z' jle .store sub edx, 26 ; wrap past 'Z' back toward 'A' .store: cmp dl, byte ptr [r9+r8] jne .fail inc r8d jmp .top .pass: mov eax, 1 ret .fail: xor eax, eax ret target byte "ZABC" check_password ENDP
What 4-character string passes the check?
Answer: WXYZ
- Each byte is Caesar-shifted +3; cmp edx,'Z' / jle decides whether the shifted value stays in range or wraps by subtracting 26 (mod-26 alphabet wraparound), then it's compared against target = "ZABC" via indexed pointer [r9+r8]. - To invert, subtract 3 from each target byte and add 26 back whenever the result underflows below 'A': Z-3='W', A-3 wraps to 'X', B-3 wraps to 'Y', C-3 wraps to 'Z'. - That gives input WXYZ, which the forward shift turns into ZABC, matching the target and returning eax=1.
